aria: Animated recap of the Spurs' 114 to 91 home win over the Pelicans: Victor Wembanyama's step-back 3-pointer with 6:29 left, his 50th point, that made it 108 to 82, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Wembanyama's 50 points with five blocks and four steals, the top scorers, how the Spurs won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Spurs' 114–91 home win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 21, 2026, from the StatMuse box score; all 114 San Antonio points and all 91 New Orleans points add up from the player lines, and the shooting totals (40 of 89, 19 of 56 from three, 15 of 20 FT for San Antonio; 33 of 90, 8 of 35, 17 of 25 for New Orleans), points in the paint (36–48) and fast-break points (18–10) match the FOX Sports team stats. The quarter scores (32–29–28–25 to 29–16–21–25) add up to both totals; the 32–29 first quarter and the 61–45 halftime score are also in Field Level Media and the AP. Assists (30–11), blocks (9–2), steals (5–8) and both biggest leads (San Antonio 29, New Orleans 3) are from StatMuse; Field Level Media also says San Antonio led by as many as 29. Wembanyama's rebounds are left off the rings: the written recaps (AP, Field Level Media, Yahoo/Express-News, Crescent City Sports) say 19, the StatMuse box says 18. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games.

Wembanyama scored 17 in the first quarter, a career high for one quarter (Express-News via Yahoo), and 32 in the first half (AP; Field Level Media), on 20 of 29 shooting overall with 5 of 11 from three, 5 blocks and 4 steals (StatMuse; Yahoo). It was his second 50-point game of the season, two shy of his career-high 52 against Dallas on Nov 4 (Field Level Media; AP). San Antonio has won 14 of its last 15 (AP). New Orleans played without Zion Williamson (left thigh), Trey Murphy III and Bennedict Mathurin (AP; Field Level Media). The Spurs play at Sacramento on Monday, Nov 23 at 10:00 PM ET (Ball Exclusives via Yardbarker; Covers).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Wembanyama's 50th point: AP: "a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 remaining in the game" (Crescent City Sports also says 6:29; the Express-News via Yahoo says 6:30 and calls it a step-back 3-pointer). The board's Spurs +23 to +26 is 105–82 to 108–82, which follows from the three. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the step-back, the passer and the exact spot are not drawn. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wembanyama’s listed 7-foot-4 and 235 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his reported 8-foot wingspan (Wikipedia), in the Spurs' home kit with No. 1 (Wikipedia) and his approved look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
